key_insight: This paper shows that Real-Bogus classification can be trained without human labels by using injected transients and mostly-bogus survey data, while still staying robust to label contamination. It also adds calibrated uncertainty estimates, making the model more trustworthy for astronomical discovery pipelines.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of building accurate Real-Bogus classifiers when reliable human labels are expensive, noisy, or survey-dependent. It aims to reduce reliance on manual annotation while improving robustness and uncertainty awareness in time-domain astronomy.
method: Train a deep learning classifier without human-labeled examples by combining injected transient signals with bogus-dominated survey data.
Design the learning setup to remain stable even when the training data is strongly contaminated by mislabeled or ambiguous samples.
Add uncertainty quantification so the model can indicate when its predictions are less reliable, improving interpretability and downstream decision-making.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates a practical path to training useful classifiers in data-scarce, noisy-label settings without expensive annotation. The uncertainty-aware design is especially valuable for high-stakes automated pipelines where confidence calibration matters.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing injected transients, bogus survey data, and the classifier output.

paper_title: Interpretable Human-Label-Free Deep Learning for Real-Bogus Classification with Uncertainty Quantification
paper_authors: Raphaël Bonnet-Guerrini, Bruno Sanchez, Dominique Fouchez, Benjamin Racine, Maya Guy
